title: Rural Partners Corps (RPC) - Host Site Application
description:
Note: This application is for Rural Partners Corps (RPC) host sites for the 2026-27 Program Year, featuring a December 2026 - August 2027 term of service. We welcome applications from partners nationwide. Submitting this form is a way to indicate general interest only -organizations are not committing to participate by applying. We encourage interested partners to complete this form as soon as possible.
About the Rural Partners Corps
Rural Partners Corps (RPC) is a new AmeriCorps service fellowship from Lead For America (LFA) that places locally rooted Members with rural, place-based backbone organizations.
Members already live in or near the communities they serve. They bring local knowledge, transferable skills, relationships, and a commitment to making their communities stronger.
RPC Members serve 40 hours per week from December through August, working alongside Host Site staff and community partners to build organizational and community capacity and advance cradle-to-career economic mobility for rural young people.
Who Should Apply?
RPC Host Sites are place-based backbone organizations serving rural communities or regions. Eligible entities include:

• Regional or community-based nonprofits

• Community Development Corporations (CDCs) & Economic Development Organizations (EDOs)

• Cradle-to-career partnerships & collective impact initiatives

• Community foundations & philanthropic organizations

• Tribal governments & Native-led organizations

• Local government agencies & regional councils of government

• Education organizations (K12 through Higher Education Institutions)

What Does Your Organization Gain?
Dedicated Capacity: A full-time Member focused on meaningful projects that advance your organization's priorities.
Stronger Partnerships: Additional capacity to build relationships, convene partners, and connect community assets.
Organizational Infrastructure: Tools, systems, research, processes, volunteer infrastructure, and other resources that strengthen your organization's capacity.
Local Talent: A motivated community member who already knows and cares about the place-and wants to contribute to its future.
LFA Support: Your Member receives ongoing coaching and professional development through LFA, while your organization has a dedicated LFA Program Coordinator as an additional source of support.
What Will an RPC Member Do?
An RPC Member joins your organization as a locally rooted capacity-building partner.
They are not an intern, temporary worker, outside consultant, or replacement for existing staff. Instead, they bring their skills, relationships, local knowledge, and initiative to help your organization move important community priorities forward.
Members will typically:
1. Know the Place

• Conduct community asset mapping and listening

• Learn the community's strengths, priorities, relationships, and existing initiatives

2. Build Relationships

• Engage community stakeholders and partners

• Support cross-sector collaboration and community convenings

• Connect people, organizations, and resources

3. Understand & Advance Priorities

• Support strategic planning and implementation

• Coordinate projects and initiatives

• Conduct research and organize information

• Help move locally defined priorities from ideas to action

4. Build Capacity

• Develop tools, processes, resources, and systems

• Strengthen partnership, communication, or volunteer infrastructure and engagement

• Support training, workshops, outreach, and community engagement

5. Support Cradle-to-Career & Economic Mobility

• Contribute to initiatives involving youth, education, workforce development, career pathways, and economic mobility

• Help strengthen connections across schools, nonprofits, employers, government, higher education, and other community partners

The Member's approach is: Know the Place → Build Relationships → Understand Priorities → Organize → Connect → Execute → Build Capacity
Specific assignments will be shaped by you

title: QA Engineer - COM INGLÊS
description:
SOBRE A CAPCO 

A Capco é uma consultoria global de tecnologia e negócios, focada no setor de serviços financeiros e energia, somos apaixonados por ajudar nossos clientes, temos 40 escritórios nas Américas, Europa e Ásia-Pacífico! Buscamos uma pessoa QA Engineer para definir e executar estratégias de qualidade para soluções que envolvem dados, integrações e inteligência artificial.

Principais responsabilidades

• Criar a estratégia de testes, os planos de qualidade e o pacote de testes do zero.

• Definir cenários, casos de teste, critérios de aceite e requisitos de rastreabilidade.

• Planejar e executar testes funcionais, de integração, regressão, desempenho e ponta a ponta.

• Testar agentes e fluxos de trabalho habilitados por IA, incluindo uso de ferramentas, memória, contexto, escalonamento e tratamento de exceções.

• Validar padrões de Human-in-the-Loop , como revisões, aprovações e intervenções humanas.

• Definir métricas de qualidade, limites de tolerância e critérios objetivos para aprovação de versões.

• Registrar, priorizar e acompanhar defeitos junto às equipes de engenharia, dados e produto.

• Criar relatórios de qualidade e comunicar riscos técnicos e impactos para o negócio.

• Contribuir para a automação de testes e sua integração aos pipelines de CI/CD.

Requisitos

• Experiência na criação de estratégias, planos e casos de teste para novos produtos ou plataformas.

• Conhecimento de metodologias, processos e técnicas de garantia da qualidade de software.

• Experiência com testes de pipelines, integrações, APIs e sistemas orientados a dados.

• Capacidade de escrever e executar consultas SQL para validação e análise de dados.

• Conhecimento de dimensões de qualidade de dados, como completude, precisão, consistência, unicidade, validade e atualidade.

• Experiência com testes de ingestão, transformação, mapeamento e reconciliação de dados.

• Conhecimento de tratamento de dados ausentes, incompletos, duplicados ou inconsistentes.

• Experiência na definição de métricas de qualidade e critérios de aceite mensuráveis.

• Capacidade de investigar falhas, identificar causas-raiz e comunicar riscos de forma clara.

• Boa colaboração com profissionais de engenharia, dados, produto e negócio.

• Inglês Avançado

Diferenciais

• Experiência com testes de aplicações baseadas em IA generativa e modelos de linguagem.

• Conhecimento de avaliação de conteúdos gerados por IA, incluindo groundedness, relevância, segurança, toxicidade e alucinações.

• Experiência com testes de agentes, copilotos, sistemas multiagentes ou soluções com RAG.

• Conhecimento de Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI ou tecnologias equivalentes.

• Experiência com Power Platform, Power Automate ou Microsoft Dataverse.

• Experiência com Python ou outra linguagem aplicada à automação e validação de dados.

description:
COMPANY

NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.

Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.

ROLE

Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and someone has to prove that our AURA RF gridded ion thruster does its job.

As Electric Propulsion Test Engineer, you run the test programme that turns designs into verified, flight-ready hardware, using NewOrbit's own vacuum facilities.

Plan and build

- Design and implement test rigs and equipment for propulsion testing.

- Assemble and maintain test hardware, electronics and vacuum facilities.

- Operate the vacuum system, RF generators, high-voltage supplies, gas feed and thrust balance during electric propulsion tests.

- Run plasma diagnostics and data acquisition, then analyse the results.

- Feed findings back to the design team quickly so each iteration improves on the last.

Verify and document

- Keep clear records of every test configuration and result, giving traceable evidence for system verification and qualification.

- Work with mechanical, electrical and control engineers to integrate and test each new iteration of the ion propulsion system.

REQUIREMENTS

Essential

- Practical electric propulsion testing experience, ideally with RF generators, high-voltage power supplies and thrust balances.

- Experience with vacuum systems (pumps, gauges, valves), power supplies, fluid management (high-pressure gas tanks, mass flow controllers) and data acquisition systems.

- Working knowledge of RF gridded ion thrusters and of plasma physics, diagnostics and ionisation processes.

- A rigorous approach to test planning, data quality and documentation.

- Willingness to work extended hours on-site.

Nice to have

- Experience with plasma diagnostics such as Langmuir probes or retarding potential analysers.

- Scripting for data analysis and test automation (Python or MATLAB).

- Experience with test rig design or hardware verification for flight programmes.

We are recruiting across propulsion design and test. Apply to whichever role fits you best - strong candidates may be considered for either.

WHY NEWORBIT SPACE?

- Pioneering space technology - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO.

- Ownership and impact - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology.

- Equity and competitive salary - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success.
